text: Good afternoon. I'm calling this meeting of the Finance and Operations Committee to order. My name is Dena Griffiths, and I'm joined by Ms. Ricardi and Mr. Pepper. If we could go to public comment. Do we have public comment today? Okay. We do not have public comment, so we will skip to the minutes. May I have a motion to approve the minutes of September 1st, 2026, of the Finance and Operations Committee? So moved. Second.

Thank you very much. It has been moved by Ms. Ricardi and seconded by Mr. Pepper to approve the minutes of September 1st, 2026, Finance and Operations Committee. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. Now, if I can get an approval of the consent agenda, we will now move on to the consent agenda. May I have a motion to approve the consent agenda? So moved. Second.

And thank you very much. It has been moved by Ms. Ricardi and seconded by Mr. Pepper. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. No action items today, so we're going to move on to our information items. First information item today, item 5.01, Business and Financial Services revised policy 4125: Cash Handling Responsibility. This item is being presented by Susan Gaviny, Executive Director of Financial

Services. Thank you. Good afternoon. We are presenting the revised policy policy 4125 Cash Handling Responsibility, which was last updated by the school board on January 11th of 2022. As part of the LCPS policy review cycle, this policy has been reviewed and suggested edits are provided by staff to capture the current practices, changes, or

improvements that have occurred since the last adopted revision. If you look at the red line version, lines five through 12 added language to clarify responsibility and accountability in the following cash handling procedures. Also, lines 13 through 20, language was added to ensure that cash is kept secure and properly accounted for in both school and non-school-based locations.

Unless otherwise directed, Policy 4125 Cash Handling Responsibility will be posted on the LCPS website for community input and distributed to school board advisory committees as appropriate for review. Any necessary changes from the public or committees as appropriate, or advisory committee input will be incorporated into the red line version of the policy and then will be brought forward to the Finance and Operations Committee as an action item.

Thank you very much. Is there any discussion? Yes, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. So in the section starting on the red line copy on line 13, the changes to school-based locations, it looks like the section is just going to simply read, "Responsible parties must turn funds over to the principal or designated school official." It's all that's going to be there is my understanding. Does the title of that section as school-based locations make sense,

or should it be something like responsibility for the keeping of funds or something along those lines as to who's responsible for where the funds are going to be kept? I also would say, and I think it's fine because we have the designated school official there, I would assume most times that's a school bookkeeper of some sort who's really collecting and in receipt of funds. That is correct, financial technician. So does the title of that section make sense, or would it make sense as something else?

I think if you then look on row 18, we also identify for non-school-based locations where those funds must be turned in, and so it's identifying between if you're a school or if you're not at a school, where the funds would be turned into. And then the other part of line 13 that was struck out is really captured in the additional red line on line 11, I guess that's 10 through 12, about

having the funds turned in at the end of the school day. So section one has been revised to incorporate the timeline, and then A and B is specifically- I- ... to whom they turn it in based on the location. Mm-hmm. So I'm trying to think about- I just think it needs a little bit more specificity, even if for activities at school-based locations, activities at non.

Just the words activities at just makes a little bit clearer because when I read it, just the cursory glance, it's where do I store the funds at a school-based location? In my mind I was like, "Well, it's going in the financial technician's office. It's going in the safe." But that's not what... So that's just for me, it's just to clear anything more than anything else on this policy. Thank you, Mr. Pepper. Any other discussion? No.

Are we okay with having this item come back for action? Yes? Okay. We'll have it come back for action. Thank you. Now we move on to item 5.02, Support Services Grant of Easements at Blue Ridge Middle School for the Purcellville G Street sidewalk. This item is being presented by Joseph Pascarelli, Director of Construction. Thank you, Mr. Pascarelli.

Thank you. The town of Purcellville is seeking easement on the Blue Ridge Middle School site to construct a sidewalk on G Street. So this is on the backside of the school. And they'll have to remove a couple of trees, replace a couple trees, as well as some bollards we have back there. Although it doesn't connect directly to a walking path we have on the campus, it will improve overall pedestrian walkability in the neighborhood. So LCPS Engineering and Division Council Office has reviewed the

documents and recommend approval. Thank you, Mr. Pascarelli. Are there any other questions or discussion? No? Okay. Does everyone feel okay with having this go on consent for the next meeting? Okay. Yes. Thank you so much. We will go to 5.03, Support Services Approval of Capital Improvement Fund Transfer and Supplemental Funds Request for

View Transition Academy. This item is being presented by Mr. Pascarelli, again, Director of Construction. Thank you, Mr. Pascarelli. Thank you. As discussed at the school board work session last week, we're seeking funding to transfer funding to meet the needs of this project. Proposed funding is coming from completed capital projects as well as from the county-held LCPS

contingency fund. The breakdown of the funding, approximately $4 million from several projects which were completed under budget, and this will close these projects out. Approximately 20 million from the county-held contingency fund. This funding would allow us to keep this project on schedule and open in the FY 28-29 school year. Happy to take any questions. Mr. Ricardi. Thank you, Madam Chair. So,

can you explain to me a little bit more about the contingency fund thing? Because I get really nervous when we take money from contingency funds in general, but tell me more about this. So yeah, that's a great question. So, a few years back, the county acknowledged that we have situations like this where we may need additional funding for projects that are perhaps inserted early in CIP, or they have gone over budget for a variety of reasons. So, at that time, they set up a contingency fund for us where we could

utilize it for those situations. And, we try not to use it in circumstances where we don't have to. It's one of these things, and the county had said to us, the agreement we have is, before we use contingency funds, look at existing balances you have first, deplete those balances, and then look at contingency funds. So they created this contingency fund for these kinds of situations that we have. What's the total balance in that fund?

So what I recall, it was $50 million, and it gets replenished every year. So it's 50 million that we have in that account. The budget funds it, and then we use it as contingency? Correct. So we get- If I may. Yeah. I want to clarify. These are funds that are managed and held at the county level, so they're not within our budget at all. As Mr. Pascarelli was describing

Because they have oversight of that, then this process in terms of having to request to tap into those funds and do a transfer out of the county held contingency that's designated for LCPS purposes over to LCPS is required. Then typically what they have done at year-end, based on their year-end fund balance, they use those funds as one example to

replenish the CIP contingency, and that has been the practice. So there have been other instances where we have had to request usage of the LCPS county held contingency funds, and then after that, at year-end, the county replenishes it back up to its full amount. I can't recall the exact amount. It may be 50. That's definitely something we can circle back and get you the exact amount, but it is a designated amount that they have set aside for us. I guess the question is then how...

I guess I need to understand that money flow a little bit better. It's been a long day, so I've got to wrap my head around some of this. Okay, so you're just asking for the 20. You're asking for almost 4 million of the 20, or you're asking for the 20? The total ask is 24 million. Four would come from existing capital projects, and 20 would come from the TMC fund. Okay. All right. Thank you.

Any other discussion? How do you feel about having this on consent? No? Okay. This will not go on consent, and it'll come back to us. Thank you. We now move on to 5.04, Support Services, Town of Leesburg Proffer Funds. This item is being presented by Beverly Tate, Director of Planning and GIS Services. Thank you.

Good afternoon. Thank you all. Today, we are bringing forward an item about available cash proffer funds that have been collected by the Town of Leesburg to benefit public schools. The Code of Virginia allows localities to seek voluntary contributions to offset the impact of residential development on the county, or in this instance, the town area.

To date, LCPS has benefited by about $7.5 million for projects that have been funded through these collected amounts. That includes the renovation of the Naval JROTC building at Loudoun County High School, the design for the North Star School, three walking tracks in the Town of Leesburg schools, Smartts Mill, Tolbert, and Leesburg, and seven

of the eight elementary schools. The town collects these funds from new development. They hold those funds for LCPS use, and then we identify, we collectively, LCPS, but most specifically you, the school board, identify the projects that we would seek reimbursement. We do not get the monies upfront. We have to initiate the projects, and then the town will reimburse for the full amount.

I'm trying to think what I needed to tell you. So what we are doing is we're bringing you a list of projects. Typically, it's every two to three years, and we come before you with a list of projects. What is included in your item are projects that we have identified from your adopted capital budget, as well as projects that individual school administrators have sought to see if they were potentially eligible.

From prior processes, what we have done this time to expedite the process is we reached out to the town to confirm if the projects are in fact eligible for funding. The proffer funds collected by the town cannot be used for maintenance, they cannot be used for repair, and they cannot be used for technology. Thus, when you look on the list that they've indicated that school marquees are not eligible because it's a technology.

The intent of the town-collected monies is to increase capacity. So with the ROTC program, it offered a new program to the students who live within the town. With the walking tracks and the playgrounds, these were inclusive playgrounds, so they offered additional opportunities for all of our students, more physical activity. It made our playgrounds inclusive for all students. So those are the kinds of projects that the town has indicated. It's all guided by Code of Virginia,

Code 15.2-2303. I know that Ms. Chernov, I will speak to her as the town representative. She's very much interested in the school marquee signs, but the town's review said that they do not include technology. The ask of you today is to consider all of the projects that are here. Some of them are not eligible. Harper Park asked for benches. Smartts Mill asked for a

covered courtyard so that they could have their children who are dropped off, kept out of the rain. Those are ineligible. But outdoor classrooms and the classroom addition, which are listed on the attachment, is potentially eligible. The town has since confirmed, since we posted this item, that they would be eligible. But our ask of you is to consider the items and then to recommend the projects to proceed to the school board for their action.

The town has approximately $3 million available. And if you wish to consider, as an example, the Richard and Mildred Loving playground, that's the only school that has not benefited from town proffers for an inclusive playground. That could be something. We've given you an estimated cost. If following up on our conversation last week, if you were interested in pursuing the addition at Leesburg Elementary, you could designate that some of those

proffers go towards the design of that. If you are interested in outdoor classrooms, again, we're happy to answer questions, but that is the ask of you today. And then we would come back for action on the 6th of October, ideally. Thank you, Ms. Tate. Questions? Mr. Carty. Thank you, Madam Chair. So I would love, I've already pinged Ms. Chernov about this too, because I'd love for her feedback on these items

and the prioritization of these items, because she would know best, I think, for that. So I definitely would like to see this for action next time with the understanding that we'll get some feedback from Ms. Chernov on which of these things from her schools she thinks would be the priority. So proffer funds are amazing. It's amazing to have access to them. We're really blessed here in Loudoun to be able to have that, for the towns that do that. So

I'm fully in support of this, but I want to do it under the guidance of Ms. Chernov's recommendations for where she thinks those priorities should be. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Carty. It does say at the bottom, no school-identified classroom addition. It has to be a classroom addition for whatever school is identified? So that was just an inquiry when we reached out to the town with the request.

We asked if in fact the funds could be used for a classroom addition, and they did respond back yes, because it's adding available capacity to the school. So yes, ma'am. Of course, I need to advocate for my school, so I know that Stone Bridge is having the ROTC program come in. And I assume that was all worked out, or did we come up with anything

they need another classroom, or they need anything to help them with their program? But also, I have to advocate for Broad Run as well. Anything that they need as far as any renovations. Can we do renovations or add a classroom for them or an addition? Anything like that, I'm just curious to know if either one were considered.

So thank you for the question, and I should have clarified at the outset. The Town of Leesburg collected proffer monies are for those schools physically located within the Town of Leesburg. So there are 15, I believe, including North Star. So Stone Bridge and Broad Run are not in the town, so they would not be eligible for these. That's my error. So thank you. Well, at least I got it out there. If I may, they're going to have the new ROTC program, so I want to make sure

they're all set. And as you know, Mr. Pascarelli, I'm real big on getting some renovations for Broad Run. So I just put it out there even though they're not Leesburg. So thank you so much. And I guess we'll wait to see what Ms. Chernov comes up with. Thank you. If we're all okay, or actually, we're going to wait. So it's not consent yet, right? Action. We're going to have this go back for action. Thank you so much.
And then we're onto new business. Anybody have new business? No? Okay.
